# 115 — Dependency_Resolving

Indicates that an attempt to obtain a requested application component is beginning\.

[All events](index.md) · [Dependency category](Category_Dependency.md) · [API reference](xref:Patware.Diagnostics.ApplicationEvents.DependencyEvents.Resolving%28System.String%2CSystem.String%2CSystem.String%29)

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| EventId | 115 |
| Name | Dependency_Resolving |
| Category | [Dependency](Category_Dependency.md) |
| Event class | LowLevel |
| Log level | Information |
| Status | Stable |
| Introduced | 0.0.10 |

## Usage

Import `Patware.Diagnostics.ApplicationEvents`. This example assumes an existing
`ILogger` named `logger` and caller-supplied variables for the arguments.

```csharp
logger.Dependency.Resolving(@dependencyName, @operationName, @resolutionId);
```

**Trigger:** Emit immediately before requesting the component from its resolution mechanism\.

**Message template:** Resolving dependency \{DependencyName\}\. Operation: \{OperationName\}\. Resolution: \{ResolutionId\}\.

## Arguments

- `dependencyName` (`string`): The non\-sensitive logical name of the component being resolved\.
- `operationName` (`string`): The non\-sensitive logical operation requiring the component\.
- `resolutionId` (`string`): The unique identifier of this resolution attempt, shared with its outcome event\.

## Remarks

- Use a new resolution identifier for each attempt, including retries\.
- An observed attempt that completes normally emits Dependency\_Resolved\. An observed failure to supply the requested component emits Dependency\_ResolutionFailed\.
- Cancellation or process termination can prevent an outcome\. Absence of an outcome does not prove resolution failed\.
- Registration and container validation are separate phases and are not resolution attempts\.
- This event describes one requested component, not initialization of every dependency in the application\.
- Calling this method only emits a diagnostic record\. It does not resolve components or enforce event ordering\.
